forecast-period.text: A slow-moving high pressure system over the Tasman Sea extends a ridge over eastern SA. A trough of low pressure over WA is expected to move into western SA later Sunday and over southeastern parts later Monday, while a weakening cold front crosses the Bight. The trough lingers in the east through the middle of the week as a weak high pressure system forms in the Bight.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Showers and thunderstorms developing in the west during the late afternoon and evening. Possible patchy afternoon showers near the eastern border. Maximum temperatures above average, grading to well above average about the west coast and tending near average in the northeast East to northeasterly winds, fresh at times, with local afternoon sea breezes.

Isolated showers and possible thunderstorms about the far northwest during the afternoon. Possible patchy afternoon showers on and east of the ranges. Southeast to northeasterly winds, with local afternoon sea breezes.

Showers and possible thunderstorms about the west, extending about central and southeastern districts during the day. Maximum temperatures above average, grading to well above average through central parts. North to northeasterly winds, fresh at times, tending northwesterly ahead of a southerly change moving across the west during the day.

Showers and thunderstorms in the east and north. Maximum temperatures above average. North to northeasterly winds over eastern districts, tending northwesterly ahead of a southerly change moving throughout during the day.

text.p: Showers and possible thunderstorms in the north and east, clearing from the southeast during the evening. Maximum temperatures above average. South to southeasterly winds, turning east to northeasterly in the far west. Local afternoon seabreezes.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Wednesday: 2 to 5 mm about Eyre Peninsula, Far North West and West Coast, increasing to 2 to 10 mm about the remainder of the agricultural areas, Riverland, Flinders and eastern parts of the NE Pastoral District. The chance of 15 to 25 mm with thunderstorms, most likely in the southeast. Less than 2 mm possible elsewhere.
